gameLoopReview.evidenceBoundary: Structural review only; no participant fun, balance, retention, or physical-device claim.

rejectedOnVerify.evidence: Live catalog already exposes Standard, Zombies, four authored modes, six ruleset variants, and three Operations; the higher-value gap is correctness at the new large-arena seam.

rejectedOnVerify.premise: The runtime lacks a coherent visual language.
rejectedOnVerify.evidence: One generated token source already drives game and public surfaces; a broad restyle would spend readability evidence without fixing a live comprehension gap.
Career, mastery, doctrines, achievements, missions, contracts, ghosts, duels, squads, and order evidence already exist; another treadmill conflicts with the Soul anti-pillars.
The live deterministic insight graph already ranks observed evidence locally; hosted inference would add variable cost and weaker provenance without a proven player gap.

rejectedOnVerify.premise: Repository-local authentication should unblock cloud backup.
rejectedOnVerify.evidence: CANON-045 requires Obelisk delegation; inventing local auth would violate the identity boundary, while missing provider credentials are independently tracked.

rejectedOnVerify.premise: The boot chunk is over its runtime budget.
rejectedOnVerify.evidence: The current App chunk is 462,821 bytes against a 560,000-byte hard boundary; the live late-load gap is the 90,498-byte DeathScreen chunk instead.

rejectedOnVerify.premise: A variable-cost API dominates the player loop.
rejectedOnVerify.evidence: The promoted work is local deterministic browser logic with no hosted model or per-user paid call; there is no measured token/API spend to optimize.

rejectedOnVerify.premise: Synthetic coverage can prove the larger arenas are balanced.
rejectedOnVerify.evidence: SOUL and GAME_LOOP explicitly reserve balance and fun claims for participant evidence; this audit limits itself to structural correctness and readability.

rejectedOnVerify.premise: The stale IGNIS or doctor score is itself product work.
rejectedOnVerify.evidence: Refreshing a derived report would not change gameplay or the release outcome; closeout owns live rescoring after shipped behavior is verified.

items.title: Make every enemy and boss spawn respect the live arena
items.why: The camera and simulation use arena bounds, but App still sends viewport width/height into ordinary enemy and boss spawning and clamps late-wave clusters to that viewport. BOT ROYALE masks the defect because it creates bots directly; any scaled wave mode would concentrate pressure in the upper-left quadrant.
items.recipe: Add a pure arena-bounds resolver at the spawn seam, pass arena dimensions into enemy and boss creation, clamp clusters to the same bounds, and add deterministic viewport-identity plus scaled-arena regression tests.
executionLog: L2 shipped in 0362b7c; focused arena/spawn court 32/32 and medium game gate passed.

premises.claim: Enemy spawning resolves the live arena bounds.
The camera system exposes the shared arena-bounds resolver.

L1.recipe: Replace the two spawn dimensions with arena dimensions.

L2.recipe: Add a shared pure resolver, update enemy/boss/cluster paths, and cover identity plus scaled bounds in unit tests.

L3.recipe: Add L2 plus camera-aware off-screen spawn exclusion around the current viewport and deterministic perimeter-sector receipts.

items.title: Turn Sewer Extraction into the second scrolling-world mode
items.why: Extraction's loot routes, rising alarm, and far-edge evac promise traversal, yet its arena remains exactly one viewport. Scaling without a density rule would make the larger world emptier and weaken pressure.
items.recipe: Opt Sewer Extraction into a 1.5× arena, derive a bounded linear pressure scale from arena scale in the mode runtime, preserve every unscaled mode byte-for-byte, and prove crate placement, evac distance, enemy count, and win/lock paths deterministically.
executionLog: L2 shipped in 26e5b96; mode-definition and Sewer Extraction court 19/19 and medium game gate passed.

premises.claim: Sewer Extraction declares the 1.5x arena scale.
Mode pressure derives from the arena scale.

L1.recipe: Set a 1.5× arena and retain the current enemy count.

L2.recipe: Scale the arena, add a reusable bounded pressure-scale contract, and cover traversal and mode outcomes.

L3.recipe: Add L2 plus seeded loot districts, risk-weighted crate values, and route receipts after participant pacing evidence exists.

items.title: Plot loot and evac objectives on the whole-arena radar
items.why: The large-world radar plots the player, enemies, arena, and royale flood only. On a scaled extraction map, crates and the far-edge evac toilet can be off-screen with no navigation signal, violating readable chaos.
items.recipe: Extract a pure radar-projection model, include bounded loot and exit markers only in whole-arena mode, render distinct gold/cyan glyphs with a pulsing evac state, and test edge/corner clipping plus viewport identity.
executionLog: L2 shipped in 96495ef/48c0c62; focused radar and arena-wiring court 37/37 and medium game gate passed.

premises.claim: The radar has an explicit loot marker contract.
The radar has an explicit extraction-exit marker contract.

L1.recipe: Paint crate and exit dots directly in the existing radar block.

L2.recipe: Create a pure bounded radar-objective model, render distinct accessible markers, and add regression coverage.

L3.recipe: Add L2 plus distance/bearing labels and priority collapse after real mobile comprehension evidence.

items.title: Move collapsed secondary analysis off the immediate death beat
items.why: DeathScreen is 1,611 source lines and its production chunk is 90,498 bytes. A large collapsed secondary-analysis panel is compiled into the same chunk as the one-verdict and run-the-fix controls even when the player never opens it.
items.recipe: Extract the secondary-analysis body into a lazy component loaded on first disclosure, preserve all evidence wording and actions, add pending/error recovery through AsyncPanelBoundary, and verify the DeathScreen chunk shrinks without changing the immediate rematch path.
executionLog: L2 shipped in 48c0c62; death-flow court passed, strict focused lint passed, and the immediate DeathScreen chunk fell from 90,498 to 73,326 bytes.

premises.claim: DeathScreen has a first-open lazy secondary-analysis boundary.

L1.recipe: Lazy-load the existing community and playtest subpanels.

L2.recipe: Extract the complete collapsed secondary-analysis body behind a first-open lazy boundary and preserve behavior with focused tests.

L3.recipe: Add L2 plus move secondary-only model builders and imports into the deferred chunk after profiling their shared dependencies.
